edges.title: Mary Stuart’s speech becomes a concert aria

works.to: Eilende Wolken, Segler der Lüfte, Op. 18

edges.claim: When the contralto of the Mass in E♭ asked for a grand dramatic aria, Beach set Mary Stuart’s “Eilende Wolken” from Schiller’s play for alto and orchestra. Walter Damrosch and the New York Symphony Society gave it on 2–3 December 1892, the first work by a woman that society had played.

sources.title: Cheryl Gillard, ‘Beach, Amy Cheney’, Women in World History (Encyclopedia.com)

edges.title: The New World prompts an Irish answer
edges.claim: Dvořák told the New York Herald in May 1893 that American composers could build on Negro melodies. In December Beach heard the New World in Boston and wrote in her journal that it lacked “the dark, tragic, side!” She told the Boston Herald that Northerners would more likely draw on old English, Scotch or Irish songs. Shortly afterwards she began a symphony on Irish tunes.

sources.title: David Weininger, ‘In a rare concert, the return of Amy Beach’, Boston Globe, 31 July 2019
sources.locator: December 1893 journal entry on the New World

edges.title: Thrush songs written down at MacDowell

works.to: A Hermit Thrush at Eve and A Hermit Thrush at Morn, Op. 92

edges.claim: In the summer of 1921, at the MacDowell Colony, Beach transcribed hermit thrush songs and built two piano pieces on them. A footnote to Hermit Thrush at Morn calls the bird-calls “exact notations of hermit thrush songs, in the original keys, but an octave lower”.

sources.title: MacDowell: The Bird Known Best by Composer Amy Beach
sources.locator: Summer 1921; Beach’s handwritten note on the score

sources.title: IMSLP: Hermit Thrush, Op. 92 (A. P. Schmidt, 1922)

edges.title: Brahms’s quintet finale supplies her theme

works.from: Piano Quintet in F minor, Op. 34, finale (second theme, bar 94)
works.to: Piano Quintet in F♯ minor, Op. 67, first movement

edges.claim: The main theme of Beach’s first movement, first heard on the first violin, is an explicit reference to the second theme of Brahms’s quintet finale. Its falling phrases return in all three movements, and in the coda it appears in octaves in the strings, as in Brahms’s coda.

sources.title: Hyperion Records: Piano Quintet in F sharp minor, Op 67, notes by Nigel Simeone
sources.locator: Brahms theme from the finale, bar 94; coda in octaves
